initial_observation.encounter_context: admitted to the Clinic of Cranio-Maxillofacial and Oral Surgery and Implantology, Medical University of Warsaw, because of a skin tumor in the right parotideomasseteric region
initial_observation.chief_complaint: skin tumor in the right parotideomasseteric region
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: At first, the patient had well-defined skin redness of 10 × 15 mm, 6 months earlier; biopsy suggested discoid lupus erythematosus and treatment with Arechin was started; after 4 months, there was significant progression and dynamic tumor growth
presenting_symptoms: well-demarcated exophytic skin tumor with irregular surface without ulceration, measuring 50 × 70 mm in the right parotideomasseteric region
no pain related to the tumor
no impaired sensation on the skin of the face
no evidence of facial nerve palsy
known_prior_history: skin redness in the same region 6 months earlier
diagnosis of discoid lupus erythematosus after biopsy
treatment with Arechin, 250 mg orally, twice a day

evidence_items.source_text: On admission, a well-demarcated exophytic skin tumor with irregular surface without ulceration, measuring 50 × 70 mm (Fig. 1), was observed in the right parotideomasseteric region.
Local anesthesia was induced for a histopathological examination that later indicated the presence of pilomatrix carcinoma (trichilemmal carcinoma) in the tumor specimen.

the biopsy material was submitted to another facility, wherein microscopic imaging clearly indicated the presence of anaplastic large cells in the dermis and subcutaneous tissue, characterized by the following immunohistochemistry: LCA+, CD30+, ALK-, CD3+ (weak membrane reaction), CD5-, CKAE1/3, MELAN A-, S100-, and Ki67+++ in about 90% of cells.
To rule out systemic anaplastic large-cell lymphoma, which involves locations other than the skin, trepanobiopsy of bone marrow was performed, and the image indicated no lymphoma infiltration.

Diagnosis of potential lymphoma infiltration was further performed with computed tomography (CT) scans of the chest, abdominal cavity, and neck and detailed assessment of the nasopharynx (Fig. 2). CT confirmed the absence of lymphoma foci in other organs, which led to the definitive diagnosis of C-ALCL.

The patient underwent 4 chemotherapy cycles consisting of intravenous vincristine 2 mg, doxorubicin 90 mg, endoxan 1400 mg, Dexaven 18 mg, and Zofran 8 mg. Blood parameters were monitored throughout the treatment period. During chemotherapy, gradual tumor regression was observed (Fig. 3A and B), and 1 year after the first cycle of chemotherapy, complete remission was achieved.
At 5 years after the end of treatment, no recurrent lymphoma was evident (Fig. 4A and B).
